claims.claim: Section 102(b)(2): where the employer company elected the capital gains track and the trustee held the shares to the end of the period, the employee income is treated as a capital gain and taxed at 25%. There is no controlling-shareholder variant of this rate inside Section 102.

claims.claim: Section 102(a) "end of the period": 24 months from the day the shares were allotted and deposited with a trustee on the capital gains track, and 12 months on the employment income track. It is NOT counted from the end of the tax year of grant (that was the pre-2003 wording).

claims.claim: Section 102(b)(3): for a company whose shares are LISTED on a stock exchange at the grant date, or registered for trading within 90 days after the grant,, the capital-gains track still applies but the gain is mandatorily bifurcated. The ordinary-income component equals the average closing share value over the 30 trading days preceding the grant date (less any exercise price) and is taxed at marginal rates + Bituach Leumi + health + surtax; only the excess over that grant-date average is taxed at 25%. Private companies at grant are taxed at a flat 25% on the whole gain.
claims.raw_snippet: היתה המניה המוקצית מניה הרשומה למסחר בבורסה, או מניה בחברה שמניותיה נרשמו למסחר בתוך 90 ימים ממועד ההקצאה, יראו את חלק שווי ההטבה בגובה ממוצע שוויין של מניות החברה בבורסה בתום שלושים ימי המסחר שקדמו להקצאה, או בתום שלושים ימי המסחר שלאחר הרישום למסחר כאמור, לפי הענין, בניכוי ההוצאות, כהכנסה לפי סעיף 2(1) או (2) לפי הענין, ואת יתרת שווי ההטבה כרווח הון החייב במס בשיעור של 25%
claims.source_name: Baker McKenzie Global Equity Matrix - Israel RS/RSU (Section 102(b)(3))
claims.note: The 30-day-preceding-grant ordinary-income component under the capital-gains track for listed companies is the §102(b)(3) rule; the income-track 30-day-preceding-settlement average is the separate Baker McKenzie RSU claim already in this file. 90-day-after-grant arm added per expert review.

claims.claim: Under Section 102(b)(2) the capital-track benefit is characterised as a CAPITAL GAIN, not as income under Section 2(1)/2(2). Bituach Leumi and health tax attach to employment income, so they do not apply on the capital track, whereas 102(b)(1), 102(b)(3), 102(b)(4) and Section 3(i) produce Section 2(1)/2(2) income and do.
claims.raw_snippet: יראו את הכנסתו של העובד כרווח הון בסכום שווי ההטבה, והוא יחויב עליו במס בשיעור של 25%

claims.claim: Section 102(a) defines "employee" as including an office holder in the company but EXCLUDING a controlling shareholder, so a 10%+ holder is outside Section 102 entirely and is taxed at marginal rates under Section 3(i) / Section 2(1)-(2), not at 25% and not at 30%.
claims.raw_snippet: ”עובד“ – לרבות נושא משרה בחברה, אך למעט בעל שליטה

claims.claim: Section 102(b)(4): where the capital gains track was elected and the realisation date falls before the end of the period, the entire benefit is treated as income under Section 2(1) or 2(2), that is employment income at marginal rates plus Bituach Leumi, health and surtax.
claims.raw_snippet: על אף האמור בסעיף זה, בחרה החברה במסלול רווח הון ומועד המימוש חל לפני תום התקופה, יראו את הכנסתו של העובד כהכנסה

claims.claim: Section 102 plan grants can only be made starting 30 days AFTER the plan is submitted to the ITA (not 30 days after board approval). Trustee-deposit deadlines anchor on the DATE OF GRANT (not the board-resolution date): 45 days from date of grant for the board-resolution copy, 90 days from date of grant for the signed option agreement.
claims.raw_snippet: within 45 days and 90 days, respectively, from the date of grant
claims.note: Corrected from prior 'deposit within 30 days of board approval' wording in the v1.0.2 reference file. Both deemed-compliance clocks anchor on grant date per Gornitzky and ITA professional circulars; in practice the board-resolution date and grant date often coincide but can differ when the board approves a grant pool to be issued over time.

claims.claim: US side of the timing mismatch: for a nonstatutory stock option the US taxes income at exercise (and RSUs at vest), while Israel under the Section 102 capital gains track defers its tax event to sale, so the US tax can fall years before the Israeli one.
claims.raw_snippet: If you receive an option to buy stock as payment for your services, you may have income when you receive the option, when you exercise the option, or when you dispose of the option or stock received when you exercise the option.

claims.claim: Section 102(b)(3): for a share listed for trading, or a share in a company whose shares were registered for trading within 90 days of the allocation, the part of the benefit equal to the average value of the company shares on the exchange at the end of the 30 trading days preceding the allocation (or the 30 trading days following the registration) less expenses is ordinary income under Section 2(1)/2(2), and the remainder is a capital gain taxed at 25%.

claims.claim: Section 102(e): the provisions of Section 3(i) do not apply to an allocation of shares to employees in an employer company. Since a controlling shareholder is not an "employee" for Section 102, Section 3(i) is the regime that does reach their grant.
